title: Named, Not Restocked, Explained
subtitle: Casimir Beng, Joost Nwosu and Mirela Hanke on what naming an owner changes about a meeting-room marker caddy
summary: A research explainer from the School of Continuous Improvement on Casimir Beng, Joost Nwosu and Mirela Hanke's term-long test of Directly Responsible Individual placards on meeting-room whiteboard-marker caddies. It follows the weekly audit from the labelled caddy to the nearest stationery cupboard, then sets the caddy's stocked-rate beside what staff came to believe about it. The authors describe the pilot, the pairing and the survey in their own words.
topic: A research explainer of the paper testing whether a placard naming a Directly Responsible Individual on shared meeting-room whiteboard-marker caddies changes how often they are found stocked, set against the caddy's distance to the nearest supply cupboard and staff confidence that it will be restocked

beats.text: A placard buys reassurance. A shorter walk buys markers.
A name on a wall doesn't restock anything by itself. What it changes is how safe everyone feels not checking.
